items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: if you asked anybody, Jon Faddis or any trumpet player, or Byron Stripling or anybody like that, they’d say no, Snooky Young.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. Like a jump band. I really think it came from the rhythm section [scats] that kind of stuff. So the upbeat [scats]. Which is much more modern swing. That’s the way we still play. And people, if they have trouble with that, they have trouble with it. It’s the weirdest thing. And being around Snooky — one time my wife said, “you can never leave the Clayton band because you play the way you play because you sat next to Snooky Young all those years.” And it’s true. And I mean we solo totally different.…
Well sort of a connected question, what do you like to get from a bass player?
